Subject: MAP: POC finalization sprint — credentials, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Per our conversation, I attached a draft mutual action plan that focuses on the POC environment setup pieces we agreed would be blocking for acceptance: API key issuance and scoping, Redwood org setup, IP allowlist entries, and VPC peering schedule. The file is redwood-map-v1.0 (attached).

Top-level asks for your team:
- Confirm desired cutover window for peering (we've proposed Mar 3–4 as low-traffic window).
- Provide the CIDR ranges and public IPs you will use for peering and allowlist.
- Confirm whether you want scoped API keys (recommended) or service-account tokens via Workload Identity.

We've left acceptance criteria explicit (prefix cache checks, inference QPS smoke tests, and latency SLO baseline). If you want, we can add a single sentence on KMS key handling for logs/metrics.

Next steps: if you confirm the CIDR and window by EOD Tue (16 Feb), Priyom will finalize the network diagram and we will push MAP->v1.2 with DocuSign for signatures.

Attachments: redwood-map-v1.0.pdf (draft)

Thanks,
Soojin

Thanks, Soojin — and great demo. A few items from our security and network teams before we sign:

- We need confirmation on how API keys are rotated and whether there is support for short-lived tokens bound to a service account.
- Who will hold the KMS keys for any telemetry we export? Our compliance team prefers customer-managed KMS.
- For VPC peering, our ops team prefers to reserve .16/28 for peer-facing endpoints; will that conflict with Redwood's suggested ranges?
- Can you provide a one-page network diagram for our infra team to review?

I attached our pre-signed security questionnaire (acrobated) — items on page 2 are the blockers (KMS, audit logs retention, and data residency).

If we can get answers on these by Friday, we'll aim to sign and book the peering window for Mar 3.

-Sarah

Subject: Re: MAP: POC finalization sprint — credentials, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Sarah — quick answers inline and attaching a simplified network diagram (network-diagram-acme.png) for your team.

- API keys / rotation: We issue scoped API keys that can be rotated on a schedule or revoked via the Console API. For short-lived tokens, we also support ephemeral credentials via our token service (recommended for CI/CD). We can provide an example Workload Identity flow if you want service-account bindings.

- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (we can integrate with your Cloud KMS / AWS KMS). For the POC we can use tenant-managed keys; we'll switch to your KMS prior to any telemetry export in production.

- CIDR suggestion: To avoid overlap, we recommend peer-facing ranges in the 10.40.240.0/28 or 10.40.241.0/28 blocks. If you prefer .16/28 we can adapt — just confirm any internal routing that might NAT through those ranges.

- Audit logs retention: default 90 days; enterprise packages can extend to 365 days. We can add an export to your SIEM via the log sink.

Proposed timeline:
- Fri 19 Feb: confirm CIDR and peering contact (you)
- Mon 22 Feb: Redwood publishes MAP v1.2 with updated timeline and DocuSign
- Wed 24 Feb: Security sync (30m) if needed
- Mar 3 (proposed): VPC peering + smoke test window

Attachments: network-diagram-acme.png

Let me know if any of these need edits — happy to hop on a 15-min call.

Thanks,
Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Blake <sarah.blake@acmehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: MAP v1.2 (final) — timeline & acceptance criteria

Hi Sarah — attaching MAP v1.2 (redwood-map-v1.2.pdf) and a DocuSign link for signatures. Changes from v1.0: explicit CIDR placeholders, step-by-step peering checklist, API key scoping guide, and a two-hour rollback window for peering changes. Acceptance criteria expanded to:

1) API keyed requests return expected inference baseline for a canonical prompt set (attached as test_prompts.csv).
2) KV/prefix cache validation completes with <5% token throughput variance after warmup.
3) Latency median within agreed SLO (200ms for 128-token requests) during smoke run.

Can you confirm:
- Final CIDR to use for peering (we left 10.40.240.0/28 as placeholder)
- Who from your team will be the network contact (we need a primary and a backup)

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=prod&formId=Zx9Y-ACME-POC
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-987654

Attachments: redwood-map-v1.2.pdf, docusign-acme-poc-link.txt

Best,
Karthik

Karthik / Soojin — thanks. We reviewed MAP v1.2 with NetworkOps and Compliance. Confirmations below:

- CIDR: we'll use 10.40.240.0/28 for the peer-facing block (no internal NAT planned).
- Network contact: NetOps primary is Paul Mendes (netops@acmehealth.com), backup is Lina Ortiz (lina.ortiz@acmehealth.com).
- KMS: we'll provide an AWS KMS key ARN for telemetry export.
- DocuSign: I signed the DocuSign form this morning (see attached docusign-acme-poc-link.txt reference).

Please provision a test API key with the following scopes: inference:invoke, metrics:read. Also send the service-account flow document you mentioned for our CI team.

Confirming we are aiming for the Mar 3 peering + smoke tests; Paul will coordinate exact calendar times with Priyom.

Thanks — Sarah
